findings.issue: `validateBuildCodeCommitRecordAgainstWorktree()` requires every `facts.phase_completion.commit_records[].commit_sha` to equal current worktree `HEAD`. But the spec now defines `phase_completion` as copied from accepted PHASE_RESULT records across phases. A multi-phase build with two file-changing phases will have multiple implementation commits; only the latest one can equal `HEAD`. Earlier valid phase commits become invalid, so final `stage-result-build-code.json` is rejected for normal multi-phase delivery.
findings.recommendation: Validate each commit record exists in the worktree and changes at least one non-tracking implementation/test file. Separately validate the final accepted file-changing phase commit matches current `HEAD`, or define `phase_completion` to include only the final commit if that is the intended contract. Add a regression test with two file-changing phase commits where both commit records are present and the final HEAD is the second commit.

resolutionSummary: revise_required: implementation closes the tracking-only HEAD case but breaks valid multi-phase file-changing completion facts by requiring all historical phase commits to be HEAD.

findings.description: Spec describes a schema/contract/gate (cluster A) with soft-fail, optional, or warning-only validation — or a check that bypasses its own control switch (cluster B: soft-fail/swallow/bypass-flag terms). A gate that does not hard-block on failure allows output drift — schema-drift blocking.

Spec describes or requires eliminating internal contradictions between field contracts or rule statements (cluster A: schema/contract terms + cluster B: conflict/contradiction/duplicate terms). Multiple conflicting schemas for the same entity cause silent drift — schema-drift blocking.
